title: The sharp number of directions illuminating a convex body
decision_reason: Canonical pre-draft fingerprint, independent current scholarly corroboration, fifteen scope comparisons, separated A63 review, exact quantifier checks and rendering/link validation passed. No unresolved material matching resolution claim located. Historical full-text limits remain explicit.

problem_fingerprint.objects: For every integer d>=3, every compact convex K in R^d with nonempty interior; no symmetry, smoothness or polytope assumption.
problem_fingerprint.illumination: A unit vector v illuminates x in the boundary of K if x+t v belongs to int(K) for some real t>0. A finite set V illuminates K if each boundary point is illuminated by at least one v in V. The choice of v and t can depend on x; V depends on K. I(K) is the minimum size of V.
problem_fingerprint.target: Prove or disprove that I(K)<=2^d for every such K, with equality if and only if K is an affine image of the d-cube. The affine map has invertible linear part.
problem_fingerprint.equivalent_cover: The minimum number of positive smaller homothets a_i+lambda_i K, with a_i in R^d and 0<lambda_i<1, whose union contains the entire closed K, equals I(K). Homothets may overlap; individual rotations and reflections are not permitted. Scale factors and translations may depend on K and i.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Exact integral covering/illumination number, including nonsmooth boundary points; neither fractional illumination nor a surface-almost-everywhere, quantitative brightness, or constructive placement guarantee.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One entry for all dimensions and the equivalent illumination, exterior-point-light and positive-homothet covering formulations. No extra entries for dimension-specific or symmetry-restricted cases.

statement_sources.locator: Section 1, Conjectures 1.1 and 1.2, definitions and equation (1), internal pp.1–3.
Section 1.1, classical real illumination conjecture and preceding definitions.

nearest_existing_entries.difference: Minimizes the length of a planar barrier intersecting every line through a fixed square; it does not minimize directions that enter every boundary point of an arbitrary convex body.
Minimizes the area of one universal container for all diameter-one planar sets up to isometry; the proposed problem covers a single fixed body by finitely many smaller positive homothets of itself.

Asymptotic density of infinitely many congruent three-dimensional bodies with disjoint interiors and free isometries; the present finite covering permits overlaps and requires positive homothetic smaller copies.

resolution_comparisons.locator: Section 2.1, Theorem 2.1 and preceding paragraph; Section 2.2 Theorem 2.16
resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Survey reports gaps in the 2000 three-dimensional announcement and states the later result under md(K)=2, with minimally dependent regular-boundary normals explicitly defined.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The general historical claim is treated according to the survey’s assessment and later current formulations. The proven restricted normal/Helly-dimension hypothesis is absent from the target; original announcement unavailable.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: All compact full-dimensional convex bodies in R^3 have C(K,int K)<=14.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Fourteen exceeds eight. Equality-case classification at the sharp value is also not supplied.
Same general-body domain but a weaker numerical conclusion; no sharp 2^d or equality classification.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Uniformly bounded isotropic constants in all dimensions.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Substitution into CHMT22 yields 4^d exp(-c d) for some universal c>0, an exponential improvement already noted in RSS26, not a proof of the sharp illumination target.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: 1-unconditional convex bodies in R^3 or R^4 that are not parallelepipeds have I(K)<=2^d-2.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Coordinate sign-change invariance is stronger than no symmetry; cannot transfer to arbitrary bodies.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Higher-dimensional unconditional bodies satisfying specified full-subcube or nonzero-extreme-coordinate conditions.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Both sign invariance and the additional geometric condition remain; an unrestricted all-dimensional conclusion is not proved.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Three-dimensional convex ball-and-spike cap bodies have I(K)<=6.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Proper geometric subclass; its all-dimensional extension is separately checked in ASKcap26.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: All cap bodies in d>=3 have I(K)<2^d.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: All dimensions are covered but only convex finite unions of spikes based on one ball. Arbitrary convex bodies are not cap bodies.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Primitive polytopes satisfy the bound and equality assertion.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Every defining facet inequality must be essential for boundedness. The text does not establish a monotone reduction of all polytopes to this subclass.
These bounds are above the proposed powers of two; symmetric variants also restrict the object class.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Corrects an author name and corresponding-author metadata.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: No mathematical correction or general resolution is asserted.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Complex phase-invariant bodies, polydiscs and complex zonotopes/zonoids; distinct integral/fractional bounds.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Complex dimension n corresponds to real dimension 2n with extra symmetry. Corrected polydisc proof and fractional results do not solve integral illumination for arbitrary real bodies.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: In each fixed dimension, non-affine-cubes in a sufficiently small Banach–Mazur neighbourhood of a cube satisfy I(K)<=2^d-1.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The neighbourhood is essential and dimension-dependent; arbitrary far-away bodies are not covered.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Weighted symmetric covering attains the sharp 2^d threshold; integral consequence retains an additional logarithmic/dimensional factor.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Fractional weight cannot be counted as a number of actual directions; the exact integral result remains open.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: At each fixed dimension, a shrinkage factor uniform across bodies can achieve the universal optimum covering number.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Does not determine that optimum; an equivalence theorem cannot establish the conjectured value.

independent_corroboration.qualification: Different author groups give explicit full general statements. ASK26 and ASKcap26 are one author group; multiple versions and the ABP correction are not counted as independent corroboration.

normalization_checks: Finite V, every boundary point, and an inward ray with positive t; V may depend on K and the chosen direction/time on the boundary point.
All d>=3 and all full-dimensional compact convex bodies; equality exactly for invertible affine images of the cube.

Positive smaller homothets only, whole closed-body containment, overlaps allowed. A common scale can be obtained after recentering and enlarging the finitely many ratios to their maximum below one; no extra problem count for this equivalent form.
The vector convention is the direction of ray travel, with a point at infinity in the opposite direction. No surface-almost-everywhere relaxation.
Integer optimum is distinct from total fractional weight; no fixed brightness, incidence angle, reconstruction or efficient placement claim.
The cap-body August v3 and primitive-polytope July v1 results are scoped by full definitions; neither covers all convex bodies.
The cube needs 2^d directions because one direction cannot enter at two of its vertices; affine invariance preserves this sharp example.
